action.rationale: Fresh problem (dim=10) with full budget 100 and cheap, deterministic evaluations; no prior info is available. Per principle 1, run probes (~12%≈12 evals) to learn the landscape before committing methods.

Probes indicate weak global structure (P2 fdc_spearman=0.112) and widely scattered promising regions (top10_spread_vs_uniform=0.94) with huge scale variability (P1 log10_range=9.58), so we should hedge across strong global methods. With 88 evals left in 10D and cheap deterministic evaluations, a 3-way race (42 evals) balances exploration and leaves budget for exploitation/polish.

CMA-ES won the race and achieved the incumbent 2.41e7 at eval 21, while it is neither converged nor exhausted (sigma=2.94, popsize=10). With 58 evals left, giving it one round (~50 evals) to exploit its basin is the best bet before a final polish.

Only 8 evaluations remain (evals_left=8) and CMA-ES has stalled for 46 evaluations with no gain since eval 50 despite sigma=2.18. With a deterministic 10D problem, a short local polish from the incumbent is the best use of the remaining budget.
